title: Two paths you drew with the Pen can be joined into one
goal: Draw two lines with the Pen, pick both, and there is no way to make them one shape. The same command over two shapes drawn with the shape tools does exactly that: it welds them where their ends meet. Somebody who drew with the Pen instead gets nothing, which is backwards, because the Pen is the tool for people who are building an outline out of pieces.
notes: Found on 2026-09-15 while building 'several-shapes-turn-into-one-path-joined-where-t'. The geometry is already done and tested: PathJoin.join in Sources/PhotonzCore/PathJoining.swift welds any list of PathContent, and PhotonzDocument.turningLayersIntoPath(ids:) already ADMITS open path layers as participants. What blocks it is only the gate: EditorState.canTurnLayersIntoPath(ids:) in Sources/Photonz/EditorState+LayerOps.swift requires at least one picked layer to still be a shape (layer.canTurnIntoPath), so two paths picked together offer no command at all. Reproduced by reading that gate and by the passing test 'An open path already on the canvas joins onto a line picked with it' in Tests/PhotonzCoreTests/PathJoiningTests.swift, which only passes because a LINE is in the selection. The open question is the NAME: Turn Into Path reads wrong over things that are already paths, and Illustrator calls this Join. Whoever takes it should settle the name first, and note that Photoshop and Illustrator both put Join on Command J, which is already New Layer via Copy here.
acceptance: Picking two open paths drawn with the Pen and asking to join them gives one path, welded where their ends meet, closed if the last end comes back to the first
The command is reachable and named so a person can find it without knowing it is the same code as Turn Into Path
It is one undo step, and undo brings back the separate paths exactly as they were
The same stated tolerance applies and the question says what you will get, exactly as it does for shapes

log.note: Adversarial review before building. The mock-free question here is the NAME, and the note says settle it first. Three candidates: (a) a new top-level command called Join, (b) folding it into Combine Shapes, (c) letting the ONE command retitle itself for what is picked. (b) is out on its own terms: Combine Shapes is area work, PathCombining.swift refuses open paths outright, and PathJoining.swift's own header says joining ends and combining areas only share the word. (a) adds a second row that runs the same code and puts a bare Join two rows under Combine Shapes > Join, which is the collision the note worried about. Taking (c): Layer > Turn Into Path... reads Join Paths... when nothing picked needs converting. One row, one sheet, one undo step, and the row still says Turn Into Path with nothing picked so it stays learnable.

Second finding of the review: with two paths picked whose ends are nowhere near each other, a dimmed row teaches nothing. House style elsewhere is to dim (Combine Shapes does), but here the cheap fix is better: offer the command whenever two or more open sibling paths are picked, and when nothing welds, change nothing and say why under the canvas, naming the 2 pt gap. A command that quietly does nothing is the clumsy version.

Third: TurnIntoPathQuestion's copy is written for shapes throughout - 'Turn both shapes into one path?' and 'They stop being shapes, so the controls only a shape has go.' Both are false over two paths, so the plan needs to carry how many actually converted and the copy has to branch on it. Also found while reading PathJoin.Run.changedAnything: a single open path whose own two ends are within tolerance CLOSES by itself, so takes can be 1 with nothing converted, and the singular-shape prompt must not be reached in that case.

Built. Core: PhotonzDocument.openPathsThatCouldJoin(ids:) is the second half of the gate, TurnIntoPathPlan.converted / isJoinOnly tell a join from a turn, TurnIntoPathQuestion grew join wording and a Join Paths button, PathJoin.menuItem is 'Join Paths…', PathEditHint.justJoined and .nothingJoined are the lines under the canvas. App: EditorState+LayerOps gate now accepts two open sibling paths, turnIntoPathMenuItem retitles the ONE row, and a join that welds nothing shows the gap instead of going quiet; LayerCommandMenu and EditorCommands read the retitled row. 12 new tests in Tests/PhotonzCoreTests/PathJoiningTests.swift, whole suite green at 7793.

left rough: no keyboard shortcut for the join. Photoshop and Illustrator both put Join on Command J, which here is New Layer via Copy, so nothing was displaced and nothing was taken; not worth a task until somebody asks for it.
